# Reporting a Finding

## Procedure
1. State the question, study type and scope. Distinguish completed findings, hypotheses, planned work and limitations.
2. Tie each substantive claim to evidence and an artifact/source locator. Use a claim title only when supported; a descriptive title is appropriate for exploratory or inconclusive work.
3. For quantitative findings report effect/metric, units, observations and independent inference units, relevant baseline/contrast, uncertainty method and assumptions. Explain when an inferential interval does not apply.
4. For theoretical work state assumptions, definitions, argument/proof status and counterexamples or limits. For qualitative work describe sampling, data collection, analytic approach, evidence excerpts and reflexivity/limitations. Do not impose p-values on incompatible research methods.
5. Separate practical relevance from statistical significance. Causal wording requires identification. Avoid extending results across populations, contexts or scales without evidence.
6. Report sensitivity checks, deviations, missing evidence and negative results. Link material decisions and reproducibility commands.
7. Create exact quantitative figures with plotting tools, inspect them, and supply units, sample/context and self-contained captions. Use diagrams only when they clarify the argument.

## Deliver
A report with question/method, findings, interpretation, evidence table, appropriate figures, limitations and next action. For substantive computational work, save code/configuration and results together. For a manuscript or thesis chapter, hand off to `writing-research-papers`.
